sentences.text: Individuals of Coelacanthus grew up to 0.7 meters in length and possessed small lobed fins, suggesting they were open-water predators. Members of this genus had a superficial resemblance to the modern coelacanth Latimeria, though they were smaller and had more elongated heads.
The hollow fin rays of the caudal fin gave Coelacanthus its name.
Coelacanthus was the first genus of coelacanths to be described, occurring roughly a century before the living coelacanth Latimeria was discovered.
The order Coelacanthiformes is named after the extinct genus Coelacanthus.
The genus Coelacanthus was established by Agassiz in 1836 and named by him in 1839 according to the Paleobiology Database.
Coelacanthus is an extinct genus of coelacanths that originally appeared during the Permian period.
Coelacanthus survived the Permian-Triassic mass extinction and went extinct sometime during the Late Jurassic, approximately 145 million years ago.
The only definitive species in the genus is C. granulatus, found in the late Permian Kupferschiefer of Germany and equivalent Marl Slate of England.
